stories.title: Singapore police help with disaster victim identification in Nepal
stories.summary: A 35-member Singapore. Police Force team is aiding Nepal with disaster victim identification and drone training after the Aug 26 flash flood that killed over 1,300 people and left 5,000 missing. The team uses fingerprinting, forensic pathology and DNA matching under INTERPOL protocols to identify victims of all nationalities. Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Government have provided humanitarian aid and are support Nepal's rescue efforts, prioritising recovery and identification to bring closure to families, including nine missing Singaporeans. KATHMANDU: As rescue and relief operations continue in Nepal following the devastating Aug 26 flash flood, a 35-member team of the Singapore. Police Force is on the ground to support the local authorities with aerial surveillance and especially disaster victim identification. The team, which started arriving in Nepal from Sept 2, includes officers trained in fingerprint lifting and photography, as well as specialists in fingerprint examination from the Integrated Forensics Service under the Home Team Science and Technology Agency. The team is still sizing up the ground situation, said Assistant Commissioner of Police Patrick Tan, the contingent commander of the Singapore. Police Force (SPF) team in Nepal. “For now, we are focusing on disaster victim identification as well as training Nepali police to operate drones to support their search and rescue operations,” he told. The Straits Times. Assistant Commissioner of Police Eugene Wang, the commander of the SPF’s Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) team in Nepal, said his team’s mission is to help identify victims across all nationalities and not just Singaporeans.

stories.title: Cold comfort: Japan’s Hokkaido battles cockroach surge amid global warming
stories.summary: In all his five decades of living in Hokkaido, Makoto Watanabe cannot recall ever being confronted by a cockroach.
